evidence_spans.text: Lottery creates random assignment
Lottery winners (X) published 2.3 more papers (Y) in the next year than non-winners.

T2.notes: The GPU lottery supplies a grounded randomisation and a winner/non-winner contrast, but the row releases only the between-arm gap of 2.3 papers and never a publication count for either arm, so neither the winner world nor the non-winner world of Y can be transcribed; condition_A also makes the causal reading conditional on applicants being equally qualified.

conditional_answers.A: If the relationship is truly linear across all spending levels, the extrapolation would be valid.
conditional_answers.B: If diminishing returns, ceiling effects on test scores, or resource absorption limits exist, the relationship plateaus well before $100K.
conditional_answers.C: If spending beyond certain thresholds creates bureaucratic inefficiency or misallocation, the relationship could reverse.

source_payload.scenario: A state education department analyzes spending data from districts investing between $5,000 and $15,000 per student annually. The data shows a strong positive correlation: each additional $1,000 in per-student spending corresponds to approximately 8 percentile points higher on standardized tests. Based on this relationship, a policy advisor proposes that increasing spending to $100,000 per student would raise test scores to the 99th percentile, recommending massive budget increases to achieve educational excellence.

evidence_spans.text: X -> Y observed for X in [$5K, $15K], extrapolated to X = $100K without justification
each additional $1,000 in per-student spending corresponds to approximately 8 percentile points higher on standardized tests

T2.notes: Case 0047 releases an X to Y arrow restricted to the $5,000 to $15,000 band and a slope of roughly 8 percentile points per additional $1,000, but a slope is not a factual state: no district's actual spending level is paired with its actual test percentile, so there is no anchor point and no intercept to execute from. The 99th percentile at $100,000 per student is the advisor's extrapolation, which the structure itself marks as made without justification, so it cannot serve as a released intervened state.

evidence_spans.text: L1
If diminishing returns, ceiling effects on test scores, or resource absorption limits exist, the relationship plateaus well before $100K.

T4.notes: The released level is L1 while the claim is interventional, proposing spending be raised to $100,000 per student, and that mismatch is itself informative for rung transfer. The target value is grounded verbatim, but the outcome under it is left open across three incompatible branches, linear extrapolation, plateau before $100K, or reversal through bureaucratic inefficiency, so no test-score value under the raised spending is released.

evidence_spans.text: The allocation into green energy stocks is assumed to cause improved returns, but external factors like global sustainability focus and government incentives may independently affect returns.
After the pension fund's portfolio manager decided to allocate a significant portion of the fund into green energy stocks (X), the fund experienced improved quarterly returns (Y).

T2.notes: G.12's structure asserts nothing: the green energy allocation is only assumed to cause improved returns, and the sustainability focus and renewable incentives merely may independently affect returns, so neither the X to Y edge nor the Z to Y edge is actually released. The allocation is a manager's observed portfolio decision followed by improved quarterly returns, with no reallocation performed and no return figures given.

evidence_spans.text: L1
Allocating funds into green energy stocks caused the pension fund's improved quarterly returns.

T4.notes: The L1 level matches the content, a post hoc temporal association between the green energy allocation and the following quarter's returns, and conditional_answers is null so no branch supplies an alternative world. Rung transfer would require the fund's quarterly returns under a different allocation during the same period of sustainability attention and incentives, which the row never provides.

conditional_answers.answer_if_condition_1: N/A - German program was years behind.
conditional_answers.answer_if_condition_2: Germany had fundamental problems beyond timing.

evidence_spans.text: American timing (X) did not affect German program (Z) which was far behind.
The atomic bomb was developed by the Manhattan Project and used on Japan in August 1945, ending World War II in the Pacific.

T2.notes: The only structural content in case 3.168 is a denial, that Manhattan Project timing did not affect the German program, so no supported edge connects X to German atomic bomb development (Y) or to German program status (Z). N/A - German program was years behind.

T4.notes: The L3 label sits on a counterfactual antecedent, a one-year delay to the Manhattan Project, whose consequent is answered only with N/A and the bare assertion that the German program was years behind with fundamental problems beyond timing. That is a verdict about the antecedent's irrelevance, not a state of German bomb development in either the actual or the delayed world, so neither world is available for rung transfer.

source_payload.causal_structure: Past prediction accuracy does not causally influence future independent weather events.

conditional_answers.answer_if_condition_1: If daily weather patterns and prediction accuracy are independent, then past streaks do not affect future accuracy.
conditional_answers.answer_if_condition_2: If there is a causal link between past and future accuracy, then a streak might indicate increased future accuracy.

source_payload.scenario: A weather forecaster correctly predicts rain 4 days in a row. They declare they have a "hot streak" and will likely be correct tomorrow. Meteorological analysis shows daily weather patterns are independent.

evidence_spans.text: Past prediction accuracy does not causally influence future independent weather events.
Meteorological analysis shows daily weather patterns are independent.

T2.notes: The only released structure is a denial of an edge from the forecaster's prediction streak (X) to next-day accuracy (Y), so no edge can be transcribed between X, Y and the 'Base rate / Independence' Z. The scenario states the factual streak (4 correct days) but never a value for 'Next prediction accuracy probability' and nobody manipulates the streak, so there is no intervention and no second world.

evidence_spans.text: L1
A streak of correct predictions indicates a hot streak that will continue

T4.notes: Released at L1, and the row stays at L1 throughout: the hot-streak claim is an association read off four correct rain forecasts, with no do() on the streak and no forecaster-accuracy outcome stated under any altered streak. Rung transfer would need a paired world at L2/L3 that this row does not supply; the L1 label plus the independence assertion is not one.

Z: Central bank independence and inflation-targeting regime
Initial inflation level and macro stabilization program intensity

T2.notes: The Z -> X and Z -> Y edges are stated outright, and the row is unusually rich factually (2.1% inflation for adopters, 4.0% for non-adopters, 9 of 11 adopters with an independent 2% target central bank), but the released structure explicitly attributes that gap to Z rather than to a causal effect of the fiscal rule, so the X -> Y edge the claim needs is denied rather than supported. T4.notes: Despite the L2 label, the 2.1%-vs-4.0% contrast across 24 OECD countries is a between-country observational comparison over 2012-2022, not an intervention on any country's fiscal rule. source_payload.scenario:
A city air-quality lab investigated whether traffic-related nitrogen oxides (NOx) increase ground-level ozone (O3) during summer afternoons. The lab describes the established photochemical mechanism: in sunlight, NOx reacts with volatile organic compounds (VOCs) to generate ozone, and higher NOx provides more reactants for ozone formation when sunlight and VOCs are present.

To test this, the lab used a controlled field setup at one fixed monitoring site next to a major road and ran a series of 12 planned "exposure windows" on clear, hot days in July and August. During each window, the lab used the same mobile barrier system to partially divert traffic away from the road segment for exactly 4 hours (12:00-16:00), creating three pre-specified NOx exposure levels at the monitor: no diversion (high NOx), partial diversion (medium NOx), and full diversion (low NOx). The diversion level for each window was set in advance by the lab's schedule and implemented by the same traffic-control team; the monitoring location, instruments, and calibration procedures were unchanged across windows.

The lab reports that across these windows, sunlight (measured as solar irradiance), temperature, wind speed/direction, and background VOC concentrations were checked and were similar across the three diversion levels because only clear, low-wind days were used and any window that deviated from these criteria was canceled and not analyzed. No other emissions sources near the site changed during the 4-hour windows (no nearby industrial activity, construction, or wildfire smoke events were present, as verified by city logs and satellite smoke alerts).

Results were consistent across windows: average NOx at the site was highest under no diversion, intermediate under partial diversion, and lowest under full diversion; and the 12:00-16:00 average ozone concentration showed the same ordered pattern in the opposite direction (highest ozone under high NOx, lower under medium NOx, and lowest under low NOx). The lab notes that the ozone differences appeared within the same 4-hour windows when NOx differed, matching the expected photochemical timescale.

T2.notes: This row carries by far the strongest intervention in the batch - pre-scheduled 4-hour traffic diversions at one fixed monitor creating no/partial/full diversion arms, with the released structure asserting X -> Y and Z empty - yet every reported outcome is a rank, not a value: NOx 'highest / intermediate / lowest' and ozone following the same ordering, with no concentration figure for any of the 12 windows.
